name: Ruxolitinib (myelofibrosis; and PV resistant to or intolerant of hydroxyurea)
disease: Myelofibrosis (primary, post-polycythemia-vera, or post-essential-thrombocythemia); and polycythemia vera resistant to or intolerant of hydroxyurea

biomarkers.note: MPN diagnosis uses driver-mutation testing (JAK2, then CALR and MPL if JAK2-negative). Ruxolitinib is a JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor and is effective regardless of JAK2 mutation status; driver mutations are used for diagnosis and prognosis, not as a treatment gate. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloproliferative Neoplasms v2.2026.

treatmentSetting: myelofibrosis with symptomatic splenomegaly or constitutional symptoms (intermediate- and high-risk); and polycythemia vera after inadequate response to or intolerance of hydroxyurea

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: myelofibrosis with symptomatic splenomegaly and/or disease-related symptoms
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, myelofibrosis treatment pages and MS-15 to MS-17 (ruxolitinib for MF)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: polycythemia vera with inadequate response to or intolerance of hydroxyurea
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, footnote n (ruxolitinib FDA-approved for PV after inadequate response/intolerance to hydroxyurea); MS-17 (PV starting dose 10 mg twice daily)

drugs.name: Ruxolitinib

provenance.locator: MS-16 (myelofibrosis: starting dose based on baseline platelet count, 15 mg twice daily for platelets 100 to 200 x 10^9/L and 20 mg twice daily for platelets above 200 x 10^9/L); MS-17 (PV: maximum safe starting dose 10 mg twice daily)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloproliferative Neoplasms v2.2026. Myelofibrosis starting dose is platelet-count based (COMFORT trials): 20 mg PO twice daily for platelet count above 200 x 10^9/L, and 15 mg PO twice daily for platelet count 100 to 200 x 10^9/L; a lower starting dose (for example 5 mg twice daily, or 10 mg/day for platelets 50 to 100 x 10^9/L) is used for lower platelet counts, with escalation. dosePerUnit 20 mg is the single-administration dose for the platelet-above-200 stratum given twice daily; see doseModificationRules for the platelet strata. For polycythemia vera resistant to or intolerant of hydroxyurea, the starting dose is 10 mg twice daily (MS-17). Days 1 to 28 represents continuous twice-daily dosing. Do not stop abruptly (withdrawal risk); taper if discontinuing.

supportiveCare: Ruxolitinib-associated anemia and thrombocytopenia are common and dose-limiting; manage with dose modification and RBC transfusion rather than early discontinuation.
Do not discontinue abruptly; taper to avoid a symptom-rebound (withdrawal) reaction.
Screen for and monitor infections (including reactivation risks) given JAK inhibition.

monitoring: CBC with differential (platelet count guides both starting dose and dose adjustment; watch for anemia and thrombocytopenia)
spleen size and MPN symptom score (for example MPN-SAF TSS) to assess response

doseModificationRules.condition: myelofibrosis, baseline platelet count 100 to 200 x 10^9/L
myelofibrosis, baseline platelet count above 200 x 10^9/L
myelofibrosis, lower baseline platelet count (for example 50 to 100 x 10^9/L)
doseModificationRules.text: Use a lower starting dose (for example 5 mg twice daily, or a total of 10 mg/day) with cautious escalation (MS-16/MS-17). Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: polycythemia vera resistant to or intolerant of hydroxyurea

doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt or reduce dose per prescribing information for significant cytopenias; support with transfusion. Physician decides.

guideline.locator: MS-15 to MS-16 (myelofibrosis platelet-based ruxolitinib starting dose: 15 mg twice daily for platelets 100 to 200 x 10^9/L, 20 mg twice daily for platelets above 200 x 10^9/L; COMFORT trials); MS-17 (PV maximum safe starting dose 10 mg twice daily); footnote n (ruxolitinib FDA-approved for PV after inadequate response/intolerance to hydroxyurea); driver-mutation testing (JAK2, CALR, MPL)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for ruxolitinib (a JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor). Primary indication is myelofibrosis with symptomatic splenomegaly or constitutional symptoms; the starting dose is platelet-count based per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloproliferative Neoplasms v2.2026, MS-15 to MS-16: 20 mg twice daily for platelet count above 200 x 10^9/L and 15 mg twice daily for platelet count 100 to 200 x 10^9/L (from the COMFORT trials), with lower starting doses for lower platelet counts. dosePerUnit is set to 20 mg (platelet-above-200 stratum) with the full platelet strata captured in doseModificationRules. The secondary indication, polycythemia vera resistant to or intolerant of hydroxyurea, uses a 10 mg twice-daily start (MS-17, footnote n). Modeled as continuous twice-daily oral therapy (cycleLengthDays 28 for reporting, cycles null, days 1 to 28 = continuous). Biomarker context: JAK2, CALR and MPL are diagnostic; ruxolitinib works regardless of JAK2 status. histology, treatmentIntent and lineOfTherapy are VERIFY. Core textbook cross-reference is pending; grounding is guideline-layer only. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
